extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (K–12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on required and permissible features of recipients' Title IX grievance procedures, including standards of proof, procedural safeguards, dismissal rules, notice and appeals, bias protections, and related obligations for K–12 and postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may use either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred; the Department states a preference for the preponderance standard but allows recipient choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department prefers preponderance because it better promotes Title IX compliance and reporting, but permits clear and convincing only if the recipient uses that higher standard in all comparable proceedings. The second sentence of §106.45(h)(1) was revised to clarify that under either standard the decisionmaker must evaluate evidence that is both “relevant and not otherwise impermissible.” The Department also clarified that a decisionmaker “must not” determine sex discrimination occurred if not persuaded by the evidence, and conversely must determine it occurred if persuaded. The beyond a reasonable doubt standard is never appropriate for Title IX proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable proceedings (parity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must apply no higher a standard of proof to sex discrimination complaints than the standard they use for comparable proceedings; 'comparable proceedings' is not rigidly defined in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to define 'comparable proceedings' in the regulatory text, leaving reasonable determinations to recipients; comparable proceedings generally include proceedings related to other types of discrimination involving the same category of respondents (e.g., students or employees) and may include similar person-to-person physical offenses. A recipient may not apply the clear and convincing standard to sex discrimination if it uses a lower standard for comparable proceedings; if a recipient uses mixed standards for comparable proceedings, it must apply preponderance to sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required procedural safeguards in grievance procedures (§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a set of procedural protections to ensure a fair process for all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among other things, the regulations require recipients to: treat complainants and respondents equitably (§106.45(b)(1)); provide the discretion to dismiss a complaint in specified circumstances (§106.45(d)); provide notice of the allegations (§106.45(c)); follow procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions (§106.45(h)(4)) and impose sanctions only if a determination that sex discrimination occurred (§106.45(h)(3)); objectively evaluate all relevant evidence and exclude certain types of evidence as impermissible (§106.45(b)(6) & (7)); place the burden on the recipient to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence (§106.45(f)(1)); provide equal opportunity to present witnesses and inculpatory/exculpatory evidence (§106.45(f)(2)); provide equal opportunity to access relevant evidence and respond (§106.45(f)(4)); and require decisionmakers to assess credibility as relevant (§106.45(g)). Recipients may adopt additional provisions so long as they are applied equally to the parties (§106.45(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and anti-bias protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must guard against decisionmaker bias and conflicts of interest and include protections such as presumption of non-responsibility and privacy safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(2) requires that a decisionmaker not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party; §106.45(b)(3) requires a presumption that the respondent is not responsible until a determination is made; §106.45(b)(5) requires reasonable steps to protect privacy; and §106.8(d) requires training for decisionmakers on serving impartially by avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias. §106.45(i) and §106.46(i) provide appeal rights related to procedural irregularity or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to gather sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient bears the burden to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to reach a determination about whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per §106.45(f)(1), the burden of producing evidence meeting the applicable standard is on the recipient, not on the complainant or the respondent. This supports reliable outcomes when combined with built-in procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification of determination and rationale (§106.45(h)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide both parties with a written notification of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred and the rationale for that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.45(h)(2) to require written notice to ensure transparency, facilitate appeals, and assist parents/guardians and students with disabilities; notices should be provided in adaptive formats as necessary. The requirement is consistent with existing recordkeeping (§106.8(f)(1)) and is not expected to impose significant additional burden; elementary/secondary recipients are not required to provide the same degree of detail as postsecondary institutions under §106.46(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals availability and parity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer an appeal that is at minimum the same as it offers in other comparable proceedings and must provide the right to appeal dismissals and certain procedural/bias issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(i) requires that the appeal offered be the same as in comparable proceedings; §106.45(d)(3) provides the right to appeal dismissal of a complaint; §106.46(i) requires postsecondary institutions to offer an appeal based on procedural irregularity or bias or conflict of interest by the decisionmaker that would change the outcome. Recipients may offer additional appeal bases if they are made available equally to all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to use different standards for students and employees (with notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use different standards of proof for student-involved cases and employee-involved cases where appropriate (e.g., due to collective bargaining or state law), but must disclose their chosen standard in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed the 2020 requirement that the same standard be used for students and employees, citing different obligations and constraints in the employment context. Final §106.45(a)(1) and (h)(1) require recipients to put grievance procedures in writing and state which standard of proof they will use, so parties know ahead of time what standard applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissal grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may dismiss complaints in specific circumstances, including when the alleged conduct—even if proven—would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissive dismissal bases are enumerated in §106.45(d)(1)(i)-(iv). The regulations note that permissive dismissal and structural safeguards (e.g., objective evaluation, access to evidence) provide mechanisms to address complaints that should not proceed to a finding of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence admissibility and objective evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence and exclude certain types of evidence that are impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added language that evidence the decisionmaker must evaluate be both 'relevant and not otherwise impermissible' (revision to §106.45(h)(1)). Parties must have equal opportunity to present and access relevant, permissible evidence and to respond (§106.45(f)(2), (f)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain documentation of grievance procedures and related records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §106.8(f)(1) recipients are already required to keep records of grievance procedures undertaken in response to a complaint; the Department noted that providing written notification of determinations and rationales aligns with existing recordkeeping and should not impose significant additional burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations should be interpreted to impinge upon rights protected under the First Amendment; First Amendment protections must be considered when issues of speech or expression are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reiterates that the regulations are not intended to limit constitutionally protected speech, and recipients must consider First Amendment implications in defining and responding to sex-based harassment (see discussion of §106.2 and §106.44(a) and §106.6(d)).
